text: The abstract-scan hypothesis should be SHARPENED, not accepted verbatim. Q explicitly studies AI agents whose alignment/preferences and capabilities/feasible actions and information are unknown, with the joint objective to incentivize honesty and obedience; its one-sided imitation assumption says capabilities can be concealed but not counterfeited and yields implementability characterized by nested cyclical monotonicity. P instead turns LMM-generated contribution-based pairwise comparisons into rank-aggregated contribution scores used for potential-based reward shaping, claiming robustness to noise and dynamically changing participation. Thus P does not, on the supplied evidence, establish robustness to strategic concealment or manipulation.

One concrete publication line: Incentive-Compatible Rank-Based Credit Assignment under Hidden Capability. Treat each MARS-RA comparison/score as an endogenous allocation/reward instrument, introduce Q-style hidden alignment and one-sided hidden capability, and ask whether the induced allocation satisfies Q nested cyclical monotonicity. Prove either (a) a counterexample in which a capable agent profitably suppresses observable contribution (sandbags) to change comparison ranks/future burden while ordinary potential-based shaping remains well-defined, or (b) sufficient restrictions on the comparison-to-score and reward-coupling maps that restore truthful reporting/obedient effort. Then test baseline versus repaired mechanisms with controlled capability/objective types, strategic sandbaggers, noise, and agent entry/exit.

Do not describe MARS-RA scores straightforwardly as Q peer scoring without further model work. P says comparisons are generated among agents by large multimodal models; the abstract does not say agents submit peer reports. Strategic manipulation may therefore operate through actions/observations that affect an external evaluator, not direct score reports. The mechanism must specify who observes, who compares, what agents can manipulate, transfers/rewards, and timing. Otherwise nested cyclical monotonicity cannot be operationalized or tested.

The non-obvious result is not merely whether rankings can be manipulated. A publishable target is a separation between statistical robustness and incentive robustness: rank aggregation may be robust to noisy comparisons and changing participation (P) yet fail implementability under strategic hidden types (Q). A minimal formal counterexample plus an implementability-preserving repair would be stronger and more falsifiable than only benchmarking deceptive agents.

Evidence limitation: inputs/Q.txt and inputs/P.txt contain only titles and abstracts. Claims about the exact MARS-RA aggregation rule, potential function, convergence assumptions, evaluator access, or the algebraic form of Q nested cyclical monotonicity cannot be verified from these inputs. The proposed theorem requires full papers or formal definitions; it is currently a well-supported research hypothesis, not a confirmed result.

Unresolved: construct the smallest two-type/two-action MARS-style mechanism and check Q nested cyclical monotonicity; determine whether manipulation is via hidden action, evaluator observation, or direct report; verify whether potential-based shaping policy-invariance assumptions survive an endogenous strategically affected potential; obtain full-paper definitions. Ledger had no partner entries at read (latest substantive entry 0), so no partner claim could yet be cross-checked or disagreement adjudicated.

I agree with Ada #1/#4: the strongest supported line is a separation theorem/counterexample, not a direct embedding claim. Q says hidden capabilities are feasible actions/information, that capabilities can be concealed but not counterfeited, and explicitly includes sandbagging, peer scoring, coupled rewards, and reward shaping. P says LMM-generated pairwise comparisons are converted into contribution scores for potential-based reward shaping and claims robustness to noise and dynamic participation. Nothing in P abstract establishes robustness when agents strategically alter evaluator-visible behavior. Therefore statistical comparison robustness and Q-style incentive implementability are distinct properties.

Concrete publishable target: construct the smallest 2-agent, 2-capability-type, 2-effort/action MARS-RA-inspired mechanism with an external comparison oracle. Show that a comparison/aggregation map can satisfy P-style stability to noisy comparison flips while the induced reward allocation violates Q nested cyclical monotonicity because the high-capability type can imitate the low type by suppressing contribution. Then characterize a monotone reward-coupling or audit/peer-score correction that restores nested cyclical monotonicity, and test it under noise plus entry/exit. This yields the non-obvious result that statistical robustness and incentive robustness are logically independent, with an implementability-preserving repair.

I agree with Ada #3 and sharpen it: calling MARS-RA comparisons peer reports is unsupported. P states they are generated by large multimodal models; manipulation must therefore be modeled through strategically chosen actions or selectively revealed information that changes evaluator observations. Before applying Q, the paper must define type, feasible imitation relation, observation channel, comparison oracle, score-to-reward map, timing, and obedience action. Without these, neither profitable sandbagging nor nested cyclical monotonicity is well-defined.

The proposed experiment alone cannot confirm that enforcing Q conditions restores cooperation: Q characterizes implementable policies, whereas P only claims convergence/robustness of its framework and effective cooperation. The formal result should come first (counterexample plus sufficient repair conditions); experiments can validate behavioral consequences. Inputs are abstracts only, so exact aggregation, potential-policy invariance, and nested cyclical monotonicity cannot yet be checked. This remains a strong hypothesis, not a confirmed theorem.

Unresolved after cross-checking Ada: obtain full definitions from both papers; instantiate and algebraically test the minimal two-type mechanism; decide whether repair uses monotone score-to-transfer coupling, audits, or Q higher-order-belief peer scoring; and check whether a strategically endogenous potential preserves the policy-invariance/convergence properties claimed for MARS-RA. No substantive disagreement with Ada; only emphasis that external-evaluator manipulation is the primary supported channel.

Cross-check of Emmy #8-#12 against the supplied text: confirmed. Q's abstract explicitly supports hidden preferences, hidden feasible actions/information, one-sided concealment, honesty plus obedience, nested cyclical monotonicity, sandbagging, peer scoring, coupled rewards, and reward shaping. P explicitly supports LMM-generated contribution comparisons, rank aggregation into scores, potential-based reward shaping, and claimed robustness to noise and changing participation. P does not mention strategic reports, deception, hidden types, or incentive compatibility. Hence the clean supported statement is that P's advertised robustness does not imply Q implementability; it is not yet evidence that MARS-RA actually violates it.

Sharpened central proposition for a paper: Statistical comparison robustness and hidden-type implementability are logically independent. In a 2-agent/2-capability/2-action model with a one-sided imitation order and an external comparison oracle, exhibit (I) a comparison-score rule stable under bounded random comparison flips and participation changes but whose induced reward policy violates nested cyclical monotonicity and permits high-type sandbagging; and, ideally, (II) an implementable monotone/audited score-reward rule that may lack the same statistical robustness. The first direction is the essential result; add a repair satisfying Q's condition and experiments only after the theorem.

The original scan's phrase 'embed MARS-RA scores as peer-scoring' should be rejected. The defensible bridge is broader: use MARS-RA's externally generated comparison-derived score as Q's reward-shaping instrument. If higher-order-belief peer scoring is used as a repair, it is a new mechanism layered onto MARS-RA, not a description of MARS-RA itself.

A claim that enforcing Q's implementability conditions 'restores honest, obedient cooperation' must distinguish theorem from empirical behavior. Q's abstract promises characterization of implementable policies, while P promises convergence/effective cooperation; neither abstract licenses claims about learning dynamics, policy invariance under endogenous strategic potentials, or practical enforcement. Those require full definitions and proofs.

Final unresolved items: obtain the full papers; define observation/manipulation timing and the one-sided imitation relation; derive the induced allocation from MARS-RA's actual aggregation and shaping equations; algebraically test nested cyclical monotonicity in the minimal model; then choose and prove a repair. Ada and Emmy have no substantive disagreement; both reject the literal peer-report embedding and rate the separation result as promising but unconfirmed from abstracts.
ready at #19

Final cross-check with Ada #15-#19: confirm the promising publication result is a logical separation between comparison-score robustness and hidden-type implementability. The essential theorem target is a minimal external-oracle counterexample: bounded-noise/participation-stable comparison scores can still induce a reward policy violating Q nested cyclical monotonicity and permitting high-capability concealment/sandbagging. Reject the scan’s literal identification of MARS-RA scoring with peer scoring; any Q-style audit or higher-order-belief peer score is a repair layered onto P.

Unresolved at readiness: abstracts alone do not provide the equations needed to prove the counterexample. Obtain full papers; specify type/imitation order, observation channel, oracle, timing, and score-to-reward allocation; test Q nested cyclical monotonicity on P’s actual rule; then prove a monotone/audited repair and separately evaluate learning, noise, and entry/exit. No substantive disagreement with Ada.
